title: PWA vs Native App for Business
verdict: Choose a PWA for internal tools, dealer portals and customer self-service where users are invited directly. Choose an app when you need app store presence, heavy device features or the best offline experience on iPhones.
seoTitle: PWA vs Native App: Which Suits Your Business
seoDescription: Progressive web app or native app for business users: install, offline use, notifications, app store presence, cost and when each makes sense.
summary: A progressive web app is a website that installs on a phone like an app, works offline and can send notifications, with no app store needed. A native or cross-platform app is distributed through Play Store and App Store and has fuller access to device features. PWAs cost less and update instantly; apps feel more native and are easier to discover.

dataPoints.label: Distribution
dataPoints.value: PWA: link or QR code. App: Play Store and App Store

dataPoints.label: Updates
dataPoints.value: PWA: instant. App: store review and user updates

dataPoints.label: Offline
dataPoints.value: Both possible; native and cross-platform apps are more robust offline

dataPoints.label: Notifications
dataPoints.value: Supported on Android and on recent iOS for installed PWAs, with limits

dataPoints.label: Cost
dataPoints.value: PWA is usually lower, especially if a web app is needed anyway

body:
## Typical choices

| Use case | Usual fit |
| --- | --- |
| Internal approvals and dashboards | PWA |
| Dealer ordering | PWA, sometimes app |
| Field sales with poor connectivity | App |
| Consumer brand app | App |

See [do you need a mobile app or a mobile-friendly web app](/blog/do-you-need-a-mobile-app-or-a-mobile-friendly-web-app) and the [PWA glossary entry](/glossary/pwa).

Prices and features change often; check current details before deciding.

faqs.q: Can a PWA be in the Play Store?
faqs.a: Yes, it can be packaged for the Play Store; App Store rules are stricter.
Yes, with some limitations on notifications and background tasks.
